- When sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, reduce forecasted price spikes; model tends to overreact.
- If model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >80% increase in 3-5 days) and sentiment is positive, check for overshoot — cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days of price decline) and sentiment is neutral, model often undercorrects — adjust forecast downward by 1-3%.
- When sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly declining, model often overestimates future rise — reduce forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 days.
- If model forecasts a sharp spike after a recent dip, and sentiment is mixed or negative, reduce the spike magnitude by 10-20% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows persistent upward trend (e.g., >5% avg. weekly gain), model often underestimates — increase forecast by 1-3% for next 5-7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.33” or “-0.00” values, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1-2% for next 3-5 days.
